intro:
The Station (table 8, a round lounge on a space station above the Earth), seat 4 (far right), drawn facing the viewer's right, MIRRORED by the game to face the table's centre. Built the way the Transylvania cast is (`art-tools/pose_rig.py`, a short `rig_spec.json`), in the same graphic-novel style: the Headless Horseman's approved sheet is the style image, lit by the station (a cool blue Earthlight rim light and warm lamps) instead of candles.

Her look, from her character file: the lost explorer, an archetype and not a person: a bulky, scuffed pressure suit of our own design, the round helmet off and on the felt beside her (it says astronaut at a glance), short practical hair, tired kind eyes, a grin she cannot quite hide, and an oxygen gauge on her wrist. No flags, no agency patches, no real insignia, nothing from any space film, no likeness of any real astronaut.

Tags (MOTION-SPEC.md): her tells beside idles that move the same part: grinning, then hiding it (strong) beside a yawn (a glove to the mouth both times); glancing out of the window at Earth (weak) beside touching the photograph in her sleeve (a look away, softened); checking the oxygen gauge on her wrist (bluffing) beside rubbing a scuff on her helmet (a hand busy at the suit). Floating a token off her palm is C4. B3 and D4 are the big win and the crushing loss; her hands are otherwise empty.

character:
Character sheet for 2D animation rigging: the Astronaut, the lost explorer: an archetype, not a real person. Copy ONLY the LAYOUT of the FIRST attached sheet (what goes where): take NOTHING of its character. No plate armour, no surcoat, no long hair. Take the STYLE from the SECOND and THIRD attached images.

The Astronaut: a woman in her late thirties, capable and worn out, with short, practical dark hair a little flattened from the helmet, tired kind eyes with shadows under them, a few freckles, and a grin she cannot quite hide. A bulky, scuffed pressure suit of our own design: off-white fabric, padded and creased, with faded orange panels on the shoulders and upper arms, a round metal neck ring where the helmet locks on, a few hoses and fittings at the chest, padded off-white gloves, and a small round oxygen gauge with a needle strapped to her left wrist. A small creased photograph tucked into the cuff of her right sleeve. Her helmet is off: a round helmet with a dark tinted visor, scuffed, standing on the table beside her. NO flags, NO patches, NO insignia, NO lettering or logos, nothing from any real space agency or any film; not a likeness of any real astronaut.

Pure white background (#FFFFFF). Every piece separate, with a closed dark outline and a wide gap all round it; nothing touches or overlaps. No text, no labels, no frames, no cast shadows.

The angle: a gentle three-quarter view, turned about 25 degrees from front-on, facing the viewer's right. Both eyes, the whole nose, the mouth and both shoulders clearly visible. NOT profile.

Draw, all facing the viewer's right, at the same size:
- Finished heads, each with the neck and the metal neck ring: a tired, kind look; talking, mouth open mid-word; grinning; the grin half hidden behind a gloved hand
- The torso in the suit, the neck ring at the top: no head, cut off straight below the waist, the upper arms down to the elbows; NO forearms, NO hands
- Two forearms in the padded suit sleeves with gloves, the oxygen gauge on the left wrist, lying on a table, pointing toward its centre, open at the elbow end
- On its own: the round helmet with its dark tinted visor
- Four seated reference poses, waist up behind the curved edge of a round green poker table, forearms resting on its edge, hands apart, the helmet on the felt beside her right hand (the left of the picture): neutral; a grin half hidden behind her left glove; lifting her left wrist to read the oxygen gauge; glancing out of a window toward the right of the picture

A: At rest: both forearms lying along the table's edge, her gloved hands resting on the felt in front of her, a hand's width apart, relaxed and NOT touching, NOT laced, NOT overlapping; the round helmet on the felt beside her right hand; a tired, kind look, mouth closed
Peeking at her cards: her right glove cupped low over the felt in front of her, thumb lifted a little, as if shielding something small; eyes down
Checking: two gloved fingers of her right hand tapping the felt
Calling: her right glove flat, fingertips leading, pushing forward along the felt
Betting: leaning in, her right glove pushed well forward along the felt, hopeful
Folding: a small, resigned push of her right glove toward the middle of the table, palm down
B: All in: both gloves pushing forward along the felt together, her jaw set
Showing: her right glove turning palm up from the felt, as if turning something over
A big win: both arms raised high, gloved fists in the air, a huge open grin, eyes shining
A big grin breaking out and being hidden: her left glove raised to her mouth, the grin showing at its edges; her right arm as at rest
Yawning: her left glove raised to her open mouth, eyes squeezed; her right arm as at rest
Glancing out of a window at the Earth: her head turned toward the right of the picture and up a little, a little homesick; arms as at rest
C: Touching the creased photograph tucked in her right cuff with two fingers of her left glove, looking down at it, softly
Checking her oxygen gauge: her left wrist lifted to eye level, reading the round gauge on it, frowning slightly; her right arm as at rest
Rubbing a scuff on the helmet beside her with her right glove, eyes down; her left arm as at rest
Her right glove open, palm up, just above the felt, a single small plain round token hovering an inch above it in the low gravity, her eyes on it, about to catch it
Turning her head and shoulders toward the viewer with a tired, kind smile; arms as at rest
Rolling her shoulders inside the stiff suit, stretching a little, eyes half closed; arms as at rest

Facing a big bet: sitting back, eyebrows up, both gloves flat on the felt

A tired laugh, her head tipped back a little, her right glove flat on her chest

style: STYLE, the most important rule: match the SECOND and THIRD attached images (the Headless Horseman and Count Dracula, from an earlier table) exactly: the same inked GOTHIC GRAPHIC-NOVEL style, halfway between a bright cartoon and a dark painted illustration. Take NOTHING of their characters: no armour, no pumpkin, no cape, no vampire. What makes that style, and this drawing must have all of it: a thick, dark, inked outline of even weight round every shape; flat cel shading in three or four HARD-EDGED tones, the shadows deep and dark and covering a good part of each form; a little rough, dry-brush texture inside the shadows only; muted, slightly dirty colour, never clean or glossy. NO airbrush, NO soft gradients, NO smooth 3D rendering, NO glossy plastic or wet-looking highlights, NO fine anatomical detail. Big clear readable shapes and a silhouette that reads at a tiny size; grown-up proportions, never chibi, never cute. The light is the space station's: a cool blue rim light from the Earth in a great window on one side, soft warm lamplight on the other, both laid in as flat bands of colour. Quiet, strange and a little lonely. NOT a children's cartoon, NOT toy-like, NOT photoreal, NOT a 3D render, NOT glossy chrome sci-fi.

NO airbrush, NO soft gradients, NO glossy 3D look; NOT a children's cartoon, NOT cute.
